chapter: Kid Ory band personnel and repertoire
title: Norma Teagarden and the Teagarden family
summary: Smith praises San Francisco pianist Norma Teagarden and describes her musical family.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: My favorite piano player in San Francisco and she is still there and still active is Jack's sister, Norma Teagarden. I find her just a delightful player and a delightful person and her abilities just encompass everything. She can literally play everything from the classics to the rags very well and she can just, if I may be so indelicate, she can just swing her ass off. She's just a wonderful player. Just a delightful, vital force in any kind of a group. I always look forward to playing with her.
It's funny that she's never made more of a name for herself. She's not a pushy

kind of person and she would not require the roar of the crowd. She always delighted in the fact that her brother Jack was so famous. She always will tell you that their mother was the great musician in the family, the great teacher of them all. She was very proud of her brother Charlie Teagarden, the trumpet player. She had a brother that she called Cub. I believe his name was Clovis Teagarden. He went off to go straight in the business world at some point but he was apparently a pretty good drummer. So it was all in all quite a family. Indeed.
